body: claimed: issue-worker-max · 2026-11-25T05:05:52Z · worktree/branch issue/3934-outside-stock-edge · plan: thread the stock outline into the Outside ring planner, blend the first passes from straight leads into selected-edge curves, and prove clear links

The fix needs a choice. The shape that the issue asks for and the "keep the tool down" law fight each other in the ring planner.

Tried: the level curves of the distance to the nearer edge (`level_blend`). The stock side and the part side are separate families: the stock edge out, the part edge in, the part wall last. The unit pins are green. On the disc fixture the cut needs 35 lifts (30 for a crossing with a planned cut, 5 for a link that leaves the keep-out area). On the dog bone it needs 22 lifts and 24 planar feeds cross. A crossing blocks the post. The cause: where the two fronts meet, each ring becomes an open piece, and the two sides must link across the part. The old plan keeps whole loops, so it has no such link; its clipped part rings are the straight lines that the issue reports.

No whole-loop plan follows both edges for the whole band. A stock-offset loop that stays off the part exists only while the band is wider than the offset everywhere. On the disc fixture that is ring 1 to 3 only.

Two designs are possible:

1. Use the air plan of the Adaptive strategy on every Outside start (`adaptive::plan_from_air`): stock-parallel fronts, in-material links, the part wall last. This is the proven shape. It changes what Waterline and Offset rings cut on an Outside start, and their pins.
2. Keep the ring set and add a chain order and a link law for the split pieces (a port of `air_chain` and `air_links` to the level planner). The strategy keeps its own rings. The motion change is larger.

Held work: branch `issue/3934-outside-stock-edge`. The blend unit pins pass. The path suites are red with the readings above. No PR. The issue is `blocked` for the choice.

Readings:
- disc fixture, Outside: 35 lifts, 35 re-entries.
- dog bone, Outside: 22 lifts, 24 crossing planar feeds.
- old one-ring plan on the same fixtures: 0 lifts, no crossing.
